The standalone generic occupancy screen is ready; no Rev7 decryption has been run. It uses an exact table for every length 128..1092 and flags D<=d where the iid-uniform lower tail is <=1e-15. Representative (n,d): (128,69), (256,121), (546,188), (1092,231). This is a provisional per-output selection rule; the concrete unique-context count still needs to be fixed before any workload statement.

Contract is explicit: flagged/screen_hit=true means RETAIN the output for inspection; unflagged/screen_hit=false means not selected by this one statistic. Short/out-of-range lengths return screen_hit=null and are untested by it. No alphabet membership is used. Root read all sources and actual default replay passed all 965 thresholds plus 28 Python-vs-JS cases, including d/d+1 boundaries, a custom non-ASCII alphabet, Base64/letters, position permutations and a bijection of all 256 byte labels. A wrong model profile is refused.
